title: From monogenic neurological disorders to neurodegeneration: How early gene therapy successes are shaping the next wave of innovation

body_markdown:
Neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Parkinson's, and Alzheimer's remain among the most challenging conditions to treat. As cell and gene therapies (CGTs) advance, researchers are increasingly applying lessons learned from rare monogenic disorders to address the complexity underlying these diseases. Early successes in conditions such as spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and hemoglobinopathies demonstrated that targeted genetic interventions can meaningfully alter disease progression, establishing a foundation for gene replacement, gene editing, and RNA-based therapies.¹˒²


By targeting diseases with well-defined genetic causes, researchers generated critical knowledge about vector design, biodistribution, blood-brain barrier penetration, routes of administration, and long-term monitoring.¹ Today's CGTs build on that foundation, combining advances in gene editing, viral vector engineering, and cell-based approaches to address the diverse mechanisms driving NDDs and expand the possibilities for patients with limited treatment options.


## Early intervenion


A key lesson from neurogenetic disorders is the value of early treatment. Notably, patients treated before significant neuronal loss demonstrated better clinical outcomes than those treated later.3 This is especially relevant for NDDs, where irreversible neuronal damage may occur years before symptoms appear.


Consequently, success depends on generating robust safety, biomarker, and clinical evidence throughout development, exactly where integrated laboratory and diagnostic partners become essential.


## The role of safety assessment in clinical success


Safety assessment remains foundational to CGT development programs. Given risks like immunogenicity and off-target effects, regulators expect comprehensive characterization of vector biodistribution, transgene expression, shedding, and immune responses throughout development. Because NDD therapies may be delivered intrathecally or directly into the central nervous system, neurological safety evaluation and long-term durability are particularly critical. Advanced preclinical testing and translational models help identify risk early and optimize clinical strategies.2,4


## Biomarkers enable earlier development decisions


In NDDs, traditional clinical endpoints often require years to show meaningful change. Biomarkers such as alpha-synuclein, tau, and neurofilament light chain may offer earlier evidence of biological activity, patient selection, and treatment response. Rare disease programs have shown the value of early biomarker strategies; namely, molecular biomarkers, neurofilament proteins, imaging markers, and other assessments can collectively establish proof of mechanism while supporting regulatory interactions. Biomarkers can also determine eligibility for viral vector-based therapies, including pre-existing anti-AAV antibodies that may affect therapeutic performance.5


These assessments drive demand for sophisticated clinical trial testing. This means that integrated solutions supporting biomarker development and testing, along with longitudinal sample management, are critical. Global laboratory networks with specialized CGT capabilities can help maintain consistency across multicenter studies while generating high-quality data required for regulatory submissions and long-term follow-up.6


## The role of diagnostics and precision medicine


The evolution of NDD gene therapies reinforces the role of diagnostics and precision medicine. Success in monogenic diseases demonstrated that identifying the right patient is just as important as developing the right treatment. As a result, next-generation sequencing, mutation profiling, companion diagnostics, and molecular characterization are becoming increasingly central to clinical development and commercialization. Diagnostics like these often serve as the gateway to treatment, enabling diagnosis, patient stratification, and enrollment into targeted clinical studies. As CGTs move toward earlier intervention, diagnostics will play a larger role in identifying patients before extensive neurodegeneration occurs.4,5


## Investment momentum signals a maturing field


Rapid expansion of CGTs across NDDs is being driven by sustained venture capital and pharmaceutical investment, which has supported accelerated innovation and strengthened the development ecosystem. Notably, the preclinical through registrational pipeline of cell, gene, and RNA-based therapeutics targeting neurological conditions has grown 11.5% from mid-2025, to more than 680 current programs.7,8 Clinical-stage momentum is accelerating, with gene and genetically modified cell therapy programs for neurological disorders growing from 57 in mid-2025 to 97 in mid-2026, a 70% year-over-year increase.7,8


Pipeline breadth and clinical-stage assets underscore growing investor confidence in CGTs for NDDs and reflect the field's increasing maturation. Continued capital deployment and strategic investment remain critical catalysts for translating scientific advances into clinically validated therapies.


## From lessons learned to future breakthroughs


The pathway from rare neurogenetic disorders to NDDs is a translational success story that established a framework for the next generation of transformative therapies. Integrated capabilities in safety assessment, biomarker development, clinical trial testing, and diagnostics are essential to accelerating innovation and bringing life-changing treatments to patients with currently untreatable NDDs. As developers navigate increasingly complex CGT programs, laboratory partners that can connect these capabilities across the development continuum play an important role in generating the evidence needed to advance therapies from early research through commercialization. Labcorp supports this need with integrated scientific, diagnostic, and laboratory solutions across every development stage.
